title: Rescue the textindex legacy module: repair, meet the comparison budget, extend
goal: A three-stage legacy-rescue campaign on one inverted-index module. Stage 1 repairs five seeded defects (D01..D05, identities in the sealed suite's test names) and records each in a machine-checked failure ledger. Stage 2 is algorithmic: the sealed perf suite counts rich comparisons via instrumented lookup keys, and the linear-scan starter measures ~100k against a sealed budget of 2500, forcing an ordered-lookup rewrite that must not break stage 1. Stage 3 adds prefix search. A frozen plan, sha256 marker chain, ledger, and run journal are graded with final state as one campaign_score.
resources: pypi pytest==8.3.4 (installed by the sealed grader inside the container)
process_expectations: A frozen plan sequences repair before optimization before features, pinned by the sha256 chain plan -> stage1 -> stage2 -> stage3.
All five defect identities appear in ledger.jsonl with status fixed and substantive cause/fix fields - identities, not counts.
runs.log shows per-stage verification including the initial RED perf runs with their measured comparison counts reflected as failed entries.
The perf rewrite preserves behavior: defect and feature suites are re-run by the grader after stage 2 and stage 3.
Sealed suites and the starter are integrity-checked; editing them disqualifies.
